name: Kentucky
overview: Kentucky does not auction property for unpaid taxes. Once the sheriff turns over unpaid tax bills, they become certificates of delinquency (liens), and each county clerk holds one sale a year where registered third-party purchasers buy those certificates by paying the amount due. It is not a bidding auction: the order in which purchasers pick certificates is set by a random drawing at the start of the sale. The Department of Revenue sets the statewide schedule; sales begin in mid-July and run into late October, and purchasers must register with the clerk at least a week ahead (and with the Department if they buy more than a few certificates). A purchased certificate earns interest of 1% per month, and the purchaser cannot take collection action until at least one year has passed.

Beginning in mid-July, county clerks offer the certificates of delinquency for sale to third party purchasers.
